pages.text: The electric pump moves fluids through Create pipes like a mechanical pump, but it needs $(item)no rotation$(): just wire it to the network. Turn it with a wrench to choose the direction of flow, as with Create's pump.

$(l)Voltage sets its strength$()$(li)It is a $(item)100 ohm$() consumer: at 200 V it draws 2 A and uses 400 W.$(li)Its $(item)pressure$() is twice the voltage, up to a maximum reached at $(item)750 V$().

$(li)Its $(item)reach$() along the pipes grows with the voltage too, up to 6.7 times a mechanical pump's range, reached at about $(item)335 V$().$(br2)A low voltage gives a weak, short pump. If a long pipe line does not fill, check the voltage with a multimeter before adding more pumps.
Like every consumer, it stops when its network runs short of power. An electric pump in the middle of a fuel line is a good reason to keep that network separate from heavy machines.
